newsitem.title: UK: Rolling Stones to tour U.S. - British newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Rolling Stones to tour U.S. - British newspaper.

text.p: The Rolling Stones, whose combined age is now 211, are to go on an eight-month tour of the United States next summer to promote their latest album.
The band earned an estimated 250 million pounds ($414.8 million) from their gruelling "Voodoo Lounge" tour in 1995 that covered 127 venues.
"There is a new album so they will tour to promote it. It's as simple as that. It's going to be gigantic again," singer Mick Jagger's publicist, Bernard Doherty, told the Daily Telegraph.
The Stones are currently working on the album which is as yet untitled.
Ronnie Wood is the baby of the group at 50, Jagger and Keith Richards are both 53 and drummer Charlie Watts is 55.
